title: J2Place: A Multiphase Clocking-Oriented Length-Matching Placement for Rapid Single-Flux-Quantum Circuits
problem: RSFQ circuits require inserting numerous D flip-flops substantially increasing area and energy. Existing placement tools do not support multiphase clocking RSFQ circuits, missing opportunity to reduce DFF overhead.
motivation: Reduce circuit area and energy dissipation in superconducting RSFQ circuits through multiphase clocking placement.
method: Novel multiphase clocking-oriented placement framework: introduces TFFDO and TFFDE cells simplifying two-phase clock networks; uses maximum flow method for column-by-column clock distribution; applies dynamic programming minimizing vertical wirelength while maintaining fixed placement orders; proposes length-aware reordering to further reduce wirelength.
key_novelty: Multiphase clocking-oriented placement framework with length-matching and new RSFQ cell designs.
contributions: Novel TFFDO and TFFDE cells simplifying multiphase clock distribution
Maximum flow-based method for systematic clock distribution
Length-aware reordering and DP-based wirelength minimization for placement
limitations: Specific to RSFQ superconducting technology; no timing validation or detailed energy analysis reported.
primary_theme: multiphase clocking placement for RSFQ circuits
